# NOTES: *Bindle: Some Chapters in the Life of Joseph Bindle* (Herbert Jenkins, 1916; Gutenberg #33261)

Only one book in the text. Sections below are in text order. Extra front/back matter (Jenkins's other books, Herbert Jenkins's Splendid Library) is listed at the end.

## FRONT MATTER
- Epigraph: "Bindle is the greatest Cockney that has come into being through the medium of literature since Dickens wrote Pickwick Papers" – MR. T. P. O'CONNOR, M.P.
- Publisher: Herbert Jenkins Limited, York Street, London S.W.1, 1916. "Eighteenth Printing Completing 283,711 copies."
- Dedication: "TO MY MOTHER, WHO AS HER SON'S BEST FRIEND IS PROBABLY HIS WORST CRITIC"
- FOREWORD (by H. J., author): earlier Bindle "little joke" piece in *Blackwood's Magazine*; late William Blackwood urged a Bindle book; a well-known author joked publishers who write books should be put to death by the Society of Authors. Address: 12 Arundel Place, Haymarket, London S.W.; dated August 1916.

## CHAPTER I – THE BINDLES AT HOME
- Blue Boar pub, Hammersmith. Bindle and **Ginger** (freckled, gloomy, misanthropic, violent-tempered; "I don't 'old wiv women"; his wife/kids: three babies before 25 jibe; wants to "'ammer" people who say it). Bindle: "women is all right if yer can keep 'em from marryin' yer."
- Bindle's philosophy: "tack" (tact), "Gospel Bells" (Mrs. B's favourite hymn), and a tin of salmon keep wife placated. If wife nags, he'd "kill a slop" (policeman).
- Bindle's father: religious, drank "to keep the chill out"; "washed his sins" at chapel; wet his hair to prove he'd been "'mersed."
- Bindle: little bald man, red nose, green baize apron, cricket cap (blue-and-white, Cambridge blue triangles). Journeyman furniture-remover; no one has seen him drunk; loves beer and "little jokes."
- Mrs. Bindle (Lizzie): sharp hatchet face, sandy hair in tight knot; cleanliness and religion ("dirt and the Devil"); attends Alton Road Chapel; bath episode (Bindle washed boots in the Friday bath, then read paper). Her question: "Got a job?" Calls him "yer great hulkin' brute." Her sister Martha married Alfred Hearty; Lizzie regretted choosing Bindle over Hearty. Lizzie uses "Mr. Hearty" as whip.
- Home: Fenton Street, Fulham, half-house; parlour a museum with musical-box (Aunt Anne's legacy, doesn't play).
- Bindle invents job at garage (night watchman, 9 p.m.) to avoid lying home jobless; pawns Mrs. B's travelling clock (bought from workmate) for 7 shillings to pay for lodgings. Mrs. B: "Steal" remark, which plants Bindle's idea of crime.
- Stewed steak and onions (his favourite) cooked by Mrs. B.

## CHAPTER II – A NOCTURNAL ADVENTURE
- Bindle finds keys (ring tagged): property of **Professor Sylvanus Conti**, 13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, West Kensington, W.; reward 2s 6d. Gets duplicates cut at a stall (1s 3d asked, paid a bob). Buys electric torch, bandages (disguise), returns keys to porter. Porter tells story of motor-bus vs fire-engine collision (11 dead).
- Conti background: real name Willie Wilkins, mother Mrs. Wilkins; cockney; hypnotist; rival "Mr. John Gibson, the English Mesmerist" (also called William Gibson in text). Gold hunter watch (from "A few friends and admirers"), revolver under pillow, handcuffs in chest.
- Bindle caught in flat; Conti holds revolver, handcuffs him. Conti hypnotises him ("You are a burglar. Repeat it."), writes note to police; Bindle delivers it. Conti searches pockets; Bindle has watch, scarf-pin, sleeve-links, studs, diamond ring (omits small change). Conti lets him go.

## CHAPTER III – THE HYPNOTIC FIASCO
- Bindle walks whistling, stops coffee-stall (sausages, bacon), feeds a woman. Asks workman for police-station; gives him the note and a shilling, saying "burglary and murder"; workman takes it to police.
- Conti phones police; press (*The Evening Mail*) gets story ("MESMERISM EXTRAORDINARY"). Police court, West London: magistrate with cold; prisoner in dock (Bindle's role, hypnotised confusion). Conti, sworn as prosecutor, says prisoner is NOT the man; fiasco.
- Property returned by post (Bindle dropped parcel into pillar-box): "a-returnin' the swag by post."
- *The Evening Post* (rival of *Mail*) mocks it; magistrate: "Professor Conti sought advertisement; he has got it... a man cleverer than himself, one who is something of a humorist."
- Bindle winks at Mrs. B; "Gospel Bells" whistled.

## CHAPTER IV – THE HEARTYS AT HOME
- **Alfred Hearty** (Mr. Hearty): brother-in-law, greengrocer, two shops (Fulham High Street, Wandsworth Bridge Road); spare, heavy moustache, iron-grey mutton-chop whiskers, woolly voice; rose from van-boy; "oily" piety; "smile" (baring yellow teeth). Sucks moustache at meals. Favourite hymn "Pull for the Shore, Sailors."
- **Mrs. Martha Hearty**: very fat, wheezing, laughs at Bindle's jokes ("Oh, Joe, don't!"); says "breath that bad" to skip chapel.
- **Millie** (Millicent Hearty), 18, daughter; soprano; loves Uncle Joe ("Oh, Uncle Joe!"). Persian kitten "Tibbins" (later chapter).
- Bindle's disruptive singing of "Pull for the Shore, Sailors" at Sunday hymns; harmonium; penknife in bellows.
- Missionary/double-bed story ("missionary's bed" Mrs. B sleeps in; grandfather clock weights in tea-things); Dean's tale "If religion don't make yer 'appy, it's the wrong religion."
- Millie asks Bindle to take her to pictures on Friday, to "put on your hard hat and best overcoat."

## CHAPTER V – BINDLE TRIES A CHANGE OF WORK
- Splendid Hotel: night painting; silent workers; foreman **Sanders** (sneering, humiliating, silent insults; Bindle recalls Brazilian knife custom). Bindle claims carpentry skill. Asked to remove/replace gun-metal room numbers on No. 1 East corridor (third floor). Sanders goes to a "funeral" (his mother, Epping beanfeast per context). Beer, bread, cheese, pickles in cupboard.
- Teddy Snell (sacked by Sanders, seven kids). Bindle's childhood "carpet nails" prank as page-boy.
- Chambermaid (rosy-cheeked, from the country) scolds re numbers; boxes Bindle's ears: "A girl would have to have tired arms to rest them round _your_ neck."
- Bindle mixes the numbers (plan).

## CHAPTER VI – THE HOTEL CORRIDOR
- Clergyman (Rev., nervous, iron-grey hair, weak kindly blue eyes, carpet slippers) enters wrong room; Bindle directs him to bathroom.
- Woman in rose-pink neglige and mob cap ("Oh! Oh!! Oh!!!"); man in her bed, bald with black whiskers (Bindle: "Yer 'usband, mum?").
- Fair-haired youth in silk kimono, eyeglass, red Turkish slippers; girl in his bed. Bindle sends him into the Office of Works.
- Clergyman vs little bald Frenchman in pyjamas ("Ma femme"; room 24, vingt-quatre; Frenchman kicked clergyman); fight.
- Army man in monocle, pyjamas (room 15), man in bath-robe (room 18); trousers swapped. Bindle: "A man don't sleep in a different room from his trousers... unless 'e's a 'Ighlander."
- Deputy-manager (manager at Brighton). Fireman (ten years at hotel) explains numbers changed; envelopes on doors.
- Monday: Sanders the foreman comes to kill Bindle; Mrs. Bindle hits him with wet dishcloth, then broom; forces him to say "God forgive me." Bindle: "Religion... seems to 'ave its Bank 'Olidays."
- Bindle has new job at "well-known stores" (Harridge's Stores), pantechnicon-man.

## CHAPTER VII – BINDLE COMMITS AN INDISCRETION
- Bindle takes Millie to the pictures; Millie wants Putney Pavilion, not Fulham cinema (Charlie Chaplin). Meets **Charlie Dixon** (tall, pale, shipping-office clerk, Millie's sweetheart; train romance; Zoo half-holiday). Bindle sends them in; "Coopid" ("Funny thing me playin' Coopid").
- Millie: "I hate it, Uncle Joe" (chapel). Run home; collides with Mr. Hearty outside shop (elbow in waistcoat).
- Bindle's charity: rescued girl near Putney Pier; collected money for mate's family; did extra whitewashing nights.
- Bindle: "I wonder if Gawd really likes that sort?"

## CHAPTER VIII – THE GREAT CONSPIRACY
- Harridge's Stores furniture department; Bindle sent to Barton Bridge Temperance Fete (Barton Bridge Temperance Society, 25th anniversary, non-sectarian tradition). Sir John Bilder sends ale. Lady Knob-Kerrick insists on London caterers (limited company). Order to Harridge's.
- Pack Horse pub: landlord **Mr. Cutts** (red knitted cap hiding baldness); **Dick Little** (doctor's son, practical joker, of St. Timothy's "Tim's"; gives Bindle flask-liquor, "pure alcohol mixed with distilled mead").
- Bindle lays lemonade with spirit in stone jars; fete: vicar **Mr. Slocum** (Rev., Church), **Rev. Andrew McFie** (Congregational, Scot, "meestrust his nose"), Miss Slocum, Miss McFie, Mr. Wace, Mr. Marsh, Mr. Grint, Mr. Ash, Miss Strint (Lady K's companion), Thomas (footman), Tool (coachman), Saunders (head-gardener), Smith.

## CHAPTER IX – THE TEMPERANCE FETE
- Lady Knob-Kerrick arrives; orders fire-hose; Dick Little; Dr. Little ("Dear me!"); McFie ("Who's Your Lady Friend?"; sword-dance in pink sunbonnet); Mr. Grint quadrille; Morris dancers.
- Hose assault, McFie leads crowd, seizes carriage as barricade; police (superintendent from Ryford) hosed; fete ends.
- Bindle leaves in pantechnicon; helps people take wrong horses. Dick Little gives Bindle a sovereign; Bindle refuses ("I been paid in fun").

## CHAPTER X – MR. HEARTY PRAYS FOR BINDLE
- Mrs. B: "Mr. Hearty prayed for you... a brother fallen by the wayside, a wheat-ear among thorns."
- Bindle's theology jokes ("Suds and Salvation"; winkles; babies; Snooker and "clean stockin's on dirty legs").
- Bindle goes to Dick Little's flat, Beaufort Mansions, 550, Chelsea; medicals/students of Tim's sing "For He's a Jolly Good Fellow"; "Aristophanes" (Little's name for him); Bindle's speech.

## CHAPTER XI – MR. HEARTY BECOMES EXTREMELY UNPOPULAR
- Hearty advertised for dog, housekeeper, errand-boy, vanman, adoptive child (advert: "Apply personally with animal to Alfred Hearty, 530 Fulham High Street... Saturday at 10.30 a.m."). Dog owner (ill-favoured, dog "Lily" – mastiff/poodle/bull-terrier/pom mix). Crowd of applicants; pantechnicons (Bindle's three vans). Police inspector; Hearty's shop beset; Bindle gives pineapple to Bindle as thanks.
- Note: Bindle's vans; Putney Bridge station dog tickets; Piccadilly point duty.

## CHAPTER XII – BINDLE AGREES TO BECOME A MILLIONAIRE
- Dick Little's Sunday evenings. **Tom Little** (brother, at St. Joseph's College, Oxford). **Reginald Graves** ("Gravy"): snob, grocer's son (father grocer in midland town; Tom Graves, 60 High Street, Bingley), claims uncle **Josiah Williams** in Australia (Moonagoona). Friends: **Travers**, **Guggers** (stutters "gug-gug"; 6'3"), Dr. Peter (Master of St. Joseph's).
- Plan to humiliate Graves with fake millionaire uncle; Bindle agrees. Oxford Mail article; Graves reads.

## CHAPTER XIII – OXFORD'S WELCOME TO BINDLE
- Station; four horses (piebald, skewbald, white, pink); band ("See the Conquering Hero Comes" vs "Auld Lang Syne"); kangaroo (Horace Trent, cox, on box). Bindle in check suit, homburg, spats, cigar with red band. Newspaper and cinema men (fake, from wig-maker).
- Bindle: "So you're Polly's boy?" Mother Polly/Mary Williams.
- Dr. Peter lunch invitation, reprimand. Bungem's banquet (St. Bungem the Hospitable, quatrain). Asparagus scene. Bindle's speech (Moonagoona, eels, tom Graves grocer sand/tea). Graves flees; chased by 200 men; porter.
- Next morning Bindle leaves on 11.6 with Dick Little.

## CHAPTER XIV – MR. HEARTY GIVES A PARTY
- Friday; Bindle and Millie walk to meet Charlie Dixon. Hearty's party: guests incl. **Rev. Sopley** (ragged beard), **Mr. Flinders** (grocer, wife), **Rev. Edward Winch** (fair-haired missionary, blue eyes; camp-bedstead).
- Mrs. B's dress (black alpaca, green satin yoke). Bindle's dress suit (Oxford spoils). Bindle's speech; kiss at "Follow my Leader"; Hearty cut pineapple; "Thank you, Joseph."
- Mrs. B. has heard Sopley's invitation.

## CHAPTER XV – BINDLE AND THE GERMAN MENACE
- Ginger and Bindle at Little Compton, Suffolk, Holmleigh (house); pantechnicon moving **Henry Miller**'s firearms collection. Dove and Easel inn; **Mr. John Gandy** (landlord, velvet skullcap, Dundreary whiskers); Mrs. Gandy. Bindle's "fort" joke; Gandy pays half-crown.
- **Mrs. Grinder** (shop). Sir Charles Custance J.P. (The Towers; fierce; German invasion talk). **Sergeant Wrannock** (Suffolk). **Roger Greenhales** (Home Farm). Foreman (Brooks) insults Sir Charles and Greenhales; Wrannock falls off bicycle; called "cockie."

## CHAPTER XVI – THE AMATEUR DETECTIVES
- Night: foreman Brooks sleeps in armchair. Gandy, Greenhales, Wrannock, Sir Charles, all enter Holmleigh; foreman captures all, puts them in pantechnicon. Bindle's men (Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles, Randers). Inspector from Lowestoft. Mr. Richard Miller (new tenant). Foreman: "I'm the band, cockie." Bindle vanishes.

## CHAPTER XVII – BINDLE MAKES A MISTAKE
- West London Furniture Depository (manager); Bindle dismissed/resigns. Move from No. 181 Branksome Road (Sergeant gives wrong key 131). Mrs. Rogers (No. 129 neighbour; maid Ruthie, Mrs. Clark next door, Archie Clark on bicycle). Mr. Railton-Rogers (bald, Thames-tug, seven children: Eustace, Nelly, Muriel) lost furniture to No. 33 Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick (Mr. and Mrs. Granger).
- Epilogue: Bindle dismissed Monday; "Lorst yer job?" "Yes... it was worth it."

## CHAPTER XVIII – BINDLE ASSISTS IN AN ELOPEMENT
- Bindle tries Kitchener's army; varicose veins rejection; joins as special constable. Putney Hill beat; finds Dick Little whistling; Little loves **Ethel Knob-Kerrick**; Bindle helps elope. Guggers's Rolls-Royce. Lady Knob-Kerrick and Miss Strint (under fallen ladder). Bindle arrested by Lady K, Thomas, Wilton; inspector; she pays five pounds.

## CHAPTER XIX – THE SCARLET HORSE COTERIE
- Friday meetings at Scarlet Horse: Ginger, Huggles, Wilkes, Ruddy Bill (Sweet William), Tom Cave, Ted, Weary, Whiskers. Bindle's patriotism: "Germany wanted wot she calls a place in the sun." Ginger enlists ("rosy song").

## CHAPTER XX – MILLIE LEAVES HOME
- Cinema outings; Charlie Dixon; Mr. Hearty meets them in Putney High Street and takes Millie home. Bindle confronts Hearty; Millie: "I wish he was my father." She goes to Aunt Elizabeth (Mrs. B). Bindle: "I'll go to chapel on Sunday." Mrs. B sobs.

## CHAPTER XXI – CONCLUSION
- Millie and Charlie engaged; Charlie enlists. Mrs. Dick Little (Ettie). Bindle: "Got a job?" motif; Dick Little's joke; Ettie: "I think he's a perfect dear." THE END.

## BACK MATTER (other Jenkins titles)
- *The Night Club*, *Adventures of Bindle*, *Mrs. Bindle*, *The Bindles on the Rocks*, *John Dene of Toronto*, *Malcolm Sage, Detective*, *Patricia Brent, Spinster*, *The Rain-Girl*, *The Return of Alfred*. Splendid Library: Victor Silvester's *Modern Ballroom Dancing*, Elizabeth Silvester's cookery, W. Riley's *Peter Pettinger*, Rosemary Rees's *The Lake of Enchantment*, Winifred Boggs's *Ashmorlands*, Maude Crawford's *Kirstie-to-Me*, Sidney Cowing's *Kim Ruff*, Alan Dare's *The Isle of Hate*, Gret Lane's *The Stolen Scar*, Fred E. Wynne's *Digby's Miracle*.
